# Farida Cajee-Botes Orthotist & Prosthetist

> Farida Cajee-Botes Orthotist & Prosthetist provides individualised, clinician-led orthotic, prosthetic and medical compression care across South Africa. Led by qualified Orthotist and Prosthetist Farida Cajee-Botes, the practice offers mobile home and hospital assessments so rehabilitation can begin early, bringing professional, assessment-led care directly to patients recovering from surgery, injury, or illness. Medical compression is a dedicated specialism of the practice, with lower-limb compression garments measured, prescribed and fitted in person.

## About

- Practitioner: Farida Cajee-Botes, qualified Orthotist and Prosthetist
- Consulting rooms: Orthocast Morningside, Block F, Ground Floor, Rochester Place, 173 Rivonia Road, Morningside, Sandton, 2196 (by appointment)
- Home visits: Centurion, Pretoria, Midrand, Sandton, Johannesburg and the greater Gauteng area (mobile home and hospital service; no consulting rooms in Centurion)
- Phone (Morningside consulting rooms): 011 883 9100 (+27118839100)
- Phone (home visits, direct): 064 652 0684 (+27646520684)
- Email: care@cajeebotes.com
- Approach: comprehensive clinical assessment, thoughtful prescription, and ongoing review. Devices are prescribed on clinical need, not available stock.

## Services

- Custom Orthotics: individually designed upper- and lower-limb, spinal, and paediatric orthotic devices.
- Off-the-Shelf Orthotics: prefabricated braces and supports for injury management, post-operative recovery, and sports protection.
- Mobility Aids: crutches, walking frames, wheelchairs, transfer aids, and bathroom support.
- Medical Compression (specialism): graduated compression stockings, compression pantyhose and made-to-measure compression garments for lymphoedema, lipoedema, oedema control, venous disease, scar therapy and post-surgical recovery.
- Breast & Silicone Prosthetics: breast, facial, finger, and toe prosthetics fitted with dignity and a natural appearance.
- Upper & Lower Limb Prosthetics: prosthetic limb fitting, paediatric prosthetic care, and ongoing adjustment.

## Medical compression in detail

The practice runs a dedicated lower-limb compression clinic. Page: https://www.cajeebotes.com/services/compression

- Compression classes fitted (European RAL standard, pressure measured at the ankle):
  - Class A: light support, under 18 mmHg. Tired, heavy legs; travel; mild end-of-day swelling; prevention.
  - Class 1: light compression, 18–21 mmHg. Early varicose veins, mild swelling, pregnancy-related oedema.
  - Class 2: moderate compression, 23–32 mmHg. Pronounced varicose veins, chronic venous insufficiency, after DVT or vein surgery, lymphoedema maintenance. The most commonly prescribed class.
  - Class 3: strong compression, 34–46 mmHg. Severe chronic venous insufficiency, post-thrombotic syndrome, healed venous leg ulcers, marked lymphoedema and lipoedema.
  - Class 4 (over 49 mmHg) and clinician-applied multi-layer compression bandaging available on request.
- Compression lengths fitted: AD below-knee (BK), AF above-knee, AG thigh-high (AK) with grip top, AG/H single-leg with waist attachment, AT compression pantyhose and tights, AT/U maternity compression tights. Open-toe and closed-toe options throughout.
- Compression constructions: circular-knit (seamless, finer, for venous conditions and mild-to-moderate swelling) and flat-knit (seamed, higher stiffness, made-to-measure, for lymphoedema, lipoedema and distorted limb shapes).
- Compression is measured on the leg in the morning, screened for contraindications such as arterial disease, fitted with application training, reviewed at four to six weeks and replaced approximately every six months.
- Upper-limb and body compression (arm sleeves, gauntlets and gloves, compression vests, scar and burn garments) available on request; the practice's focus is lower-limb compression.
- Compression assessment, measuring and fitting available at the Morningside consulting rooms, at home, or at the hospital bedside across Gauteng.
